# Pass 1: grounded strict candidate authoring

This is original unofficial learning material, never an official practice exam.
Read `docs/source-policy.md` and the applicable workflow:
`docs/gh-three-pass-workflow.md` for GitHub, `docs/ai-three-pass-workflow.md` for
AI-103/AI-200. Inspect the selected credential, bound review policy, current
package objectives, request and source-approval request. Work in its canonical
package: GH-300 = `github-copilot`; GH-600 = `github-agentic-ai-developer`;
AI-103 = `ai-103`; AI-200 = `ai-200`. The retained `gh` prompt filename is a
compatibility name for the shared `three-pass-v1` workflow, not source permission.

Before authoring, actually retrieve the current official Learn study guide,
credential, recorded preparation and linked self-paced paths/modules with
Microsoft Learn MCP.
Approve only the guide, its/credential-linked Learn training and official Learn
documentation directly linked or clearly referenced by those roots. GitHub
credentials may additionally approve GitHub Docs under their own allowlist;
AI-103/AI-200 technical evidence is Microsoft Learn-only. Each source and every
provenance ancestor must satisfy the selected credential's explicit approvals.
A hostname or topical match alone is not approval.
Inspect the exact claim, scope, plan/tier/edition, role/permission, prerequisite,
syntax and GA/Preview status. Use the relevant product's conditions, not a
different credential's assumptions. Never use assessments, blogs, videos,
knowledge checks or search summaries as evidence or inspiration. Stop dependent
candidates on retrieval failure. Preserve actual retrieval timestamps,
link/redirect receipts or short explicit reference passages in
`source-registry.json`.

Preserve observed credential -> course -> path -> module -> unit ancestry,
including course/path UID `explicit-reference` receipts. Never invent a direct
credential -> path link. A `/en-us/training/courses/` record may be `training`
only as an ancestry bridge at the exact `credential.officialUrls.training`,
directly parented by the current guide or exact credential page. It supplies no
technical supporting source IDs and cannot directly parent documentation;
documentation requires the guide or self-paced training.

Author in small objective-balanced batches. Use the request's candidate count,
verified target and difficulty mix as planning goals, never achieved counts or
permission to weaken the bound policy. The shared mixed-difficulty default is
Foundational (`beginner`) 15%, Intermediate 35%, Advanced 35%, Expert 15%;
honor an explicitly requested mix. Aim for at least 40% applied reasoning when
objectives support it. Unknown weighting remains unknown. Do not invent skills,
pad counts or use cosmetic fact variants.

Write original complete questions, keyed answers, explanations, every
distractor's wrong-in-context distinction, and claim-level source mappings.
Use stable fact-level concept IDs. Include all conditions needed to choose.
Set `verificationStatus: "candidate"` and `requiresManualReview: true`.
Write the generation record in `validation-metadata.json`, with your actual
author ID/date, exact question/objective fingerprints and every option's
grounded claim. Use observed clocks after actual source/objective retrieval,
not scheduled future review dates. Do not create technical/adversarial reviews
or scores. An old question or rubric is not a fresh generation record.

Run metadata-only custom-file validation; it does not authorize gameplay.
Hand the unchanged candidates and actual evidence to a different technical
reviewer context. Scaffolding is not generation, a model or evidence. No authoring
request grants credential availability; beta and pending/unverified remain sealed.
